prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it lists the order lines of the store orders (channel store) placed on 9 March 2025, with the time of each line's order and the code of the store that took it. order_ts holds UTC time: take the day in UTC, and return order_ts as it is stored. Return four columns, in this order: order_line_id, order_ts, store_code and quantity. Return one row for each order line. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, write the join from each line to its order using the line's order ID.
order_line_id numbers the lines and order_id numbers the orders. They look alike, but only the line's order_id points at an order.
starter_sql:
SELECT l.order_line_id, o.order_ts, s.store_code, l.quantity
FROM order_lines l
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_line_id
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
WHERE o.channel = 'store'
  AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-09 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-10 00:00:00'
why_this_works: order_lines.order_id is the foreign key to orders; order_line_id only numbers the lines, so matching on it pairs lines with unrelated orders and their times.
